title: Brasília (Pilot Plan)
summary: Brasília, Brazil's capital, was created from nothing in the centre of the country in 1956-1960 by the planner Lucio Costa and the architect Oscar Niemeyer. UNESCO calls it a landmark in the history of town planning. The pin and 3D model are its Metropolitan Cathedral, a circular structure 70 m across and 40 m high with 16 columns, finished in 1970.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO gives the creation of the capital as 1956 in English and 1956-1960 in French and Spanish. End is the present: the city is the capital. The cathedral's own dates (1958-1970) are in the model phases.

reviewer_note: The record is the city (UNESCO Pilot Plan), but the model describes ONE structure, the Metropolitan Cathedral, so the pin sits on the cathedral. Shape: dome (closest available to the hyperboloid of 16 members; mention for the reviewer). Height 40 m is from the Ministry of Tourism; a UnB thesis seen in search results gave 30 m but was not opened, so treat height as less sure than the 70 m diameter. Inauguration date conflicts: 1967 (Ministry of Tourism) versus 31 May 1970 (Arquivo Público DF); 1970 is used. The National Congress towers were not modelled because no opened page gave their height.
